Apple's current CEO Tim Cook and incoming CEO John Ternus spoke to Deadline about the leadership transition, Apple TV, and more. Here is what they had to say.

Tim Cook and John Ternus attend the premiere of *Ted Lasso*, discussing the CEO transition and Apple TV

The world premiere of *Ted Lasso* season 4 was held in Los Angeles last night, with both Apple's current and incoming CEOs in attendance. *Ted Lasso* returns to Apple TV on August 5 (watch link).

Tim Cook and John Ternus both wore coordinated suits, each pinning a lapel badge featuring the word "Believe" from *Ted Lasso*.

Deadline's Nellie Andreeva spoke with Cook and Ternus, asking about the CEO transition and the future of Apple TV.

Cook said: "It has been the greatest privilege of my life to be the CEO of Apple for 15 years and to work with such an extraordinary group of people. I am deeply grateful." Discussing the transition, he added: "It's all going very well. John is the best person for the job, and the transition has been excellent — whether with employees, investors, across the board."

Ternus added: "It's been amazing. What an opportunity! I'm incredibly excited. I've been at Apple for 25 years, I love this company, and to have this opportunity is beyond words."

Asked what his first task would be after taking over as CEO on September 1, Ternus said: "Stay tuned."

Discussing Apple TV, Ternus praised the work of Eddy Cue and his team, and declined to reveal any plans for change. "I'm incredibly excited about the momentum right now. There's tremendous content on Apple TV, and there's no better time to capitalize on that momentum."

He revealed he is currently watching *Silo* and *Lucky* on Apple TV. Cook said he had recently watched *Widow's Bay*, *Pluribus*, and *Silo*.

Interestingly, Cook was asked whether he would watch season 4 of *Ted Lasso* on Apple Vision Pro — reportedly how he watched season 3. He replied with a smile: "Absolutely, and I'll be lying down with the Vision Pro — there's nothing like it."

The full interview is available to read or watch on the Deadline website.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, with discounts available when bundled with Apple One.
